title: 3D Atlas: Beaumont’s Gastric Window & the Alimentary Canal
question: How did William Beaumont prove through Alexis St Martin’s gastric fistula that digestion is driven by coordinated muscular churning and chemical catalysis?
explanation: Slicing the 3D muscular tube reveals inner circular muscle contracting behind the food bolus while outer longitudinal muscle shortens ahead of it, propelling chyme through pH-zoned compartments.
limits: Travelling sinusoidal peristaltic wave along a cylindrical gut segment.

title: 3D Atlas: Ingestion, Digestion, Absorption & Egestion Across the Gut Wall
question: Why is food in the intestinal lumen topology-wise still ‘outside’ the body’s internal cellular environment until it crosses the villus epithelium?
explanation: Trace the meal along the lumen, then across the epithelial barrier. Glucose and amino acids use selective transport before entering capillaries; long-chain lipid products are rebuilt into chylomicrons before entering lymph. Water, ions and some other nutrients need no prior digestion.
limits: Topological lumen-to-capillary boundary view.

title: 3D Atlas: Antagonistic Circular & Longitudinal Muscle Peristalsis
question: Why can you swallow water even while hanging upside down?
explanation: Exploding the 3D oesophageal wall shows that swallowing is not passive gravity fall: a reflex wave of circular-muscle constriction behind the bolus and relaxation ahead of it pushes food inexorably toward the stomach.
limits: Single-bolus travelling constriction wave.

title: 3D Atlas: Regional pH Compartments for Amylase, Pepsin & Trypsin
question: Why do digestive enzymes work under different conditions in different gut compartments?
explanation: Compare illustrative activity curves as pH changes. Acid supports stomach pepsin activity; pancreatic bicarbonate is a major contributor to the different intestinal conditions. The curves are teaching shapes, not measured universal enzyme profiles.
limits: Illustrative pH curves; values vary with enzyme and conditions.

title: 3D Atlas: Gastric Mucus–Bicarbonate Barrier & Pepsinogen Activation
question: Why doesn’t the stomach’s own HCl (pH 1.8) and pepsin digest the living stomach wall itself?
explanation: Inspect the protective mucus and bicarbonate layer, alongside the chapter explanation of epithelial joins, repair and inactive protease precursors. Surface mucus cells protect the stomach lining; no single layer guarantees complete protection.
limits: Cross-sectional mucosal wall protection layer.

title: 3D Atlas: Amphipathic Bile Salts & 64-Droplet Lipid Emulsification
question: How can smaller fat droplets provide four times the interface without proving a fourfold digestion rate?
explanation: Choose a geometric division into 64 equal droplets of the same total volume. Their combined interface is four times larger. This is a droplet-geometry model, not a calibrated bile-concentration or enzyme-rate experiment; lipase supply and interfacial conditions still matter.
limits: Equal-radius spherical subdivision model.

title: 3D Atlas: Lipase at the Fat-Droplet Interface
question: Why does water-soluble pancreatic lipase act only at the oil–water surface of lipid droplets?
explanation: Inspecting the green pancreatic lipase enzymes docked around the 3D emulsified droplets shows how bile-salt emulsification multiplies accessible ester bonds for hydrolysis into fatty acids and monoglycerides.
limits: Structural interface schematic; no calculated hydrolysis rate.

title: 3D Atlas: Intestinal Villus Capillary Cage vs Central Lacteal
question: Why do absorbed glucose and amino acids enter the villus blood capillaries while long-chain fats enter the central lymphatic lacteal?
explanation: Switching the 3D intestinal villus to X-ray or Section cutaway view reveals water-soluble sugars and amino acids crossing the single-cell brush-border epithelium into the capillary mesh, while bulky chylomicrons enter the porous central lacteal.
limits: Single finger-like villus column with representative microvillus amplification.

title: 3D Atlas: Hepatic Portal Vein & First-Pass Liver Metabolic Checkpoint
question: Why does venous blood from the small intestine detour through a second capillary bed in the liver before reaching the heart?
explanation: The villus view identifies the capillary route. Blood leaving intestinal capillaries subsequently reaches the liver through the hepatic portal vein; that later organ route is explained in the chapter, rather than represented by a complete liver model here.
limits: Villus and onward-route explanation; no modelled liver clearance or sinusoidal flow.

title: 3D Atlas: C-Shaped Tracheal Cartilage Rings & Bronchial Tree
question: Why is the trachea reinforced with incomplete C-shaped cartilage rings rather than rigid solid cylinders or soft muscle alone?
explanation: Inspecting the 3D trachea and bronchi above the expanding lungs shows how C-rings prevent airway collapse during negative-pressure inspiration while letting the oesophagus bulge forward during swallowing.
limits: Upper bronchial tree and thoracic bellows model.

title: 3D Atlas: Rib Bucket-Handle Kinematics, Diaphragm Dome & Boyle’s Law
question: How does chest expansion create the pressure difference that drives air into the lungs?
explanation: The expanding ribcage and flattening diaphragm expand the lungs through pleural coupling. Alveolar pressure briefly falls below outside pressure, driving inward airflow. The displayed pressure swing is a chosen small schematic cycle.
limits: Open-air breathing schematic; the pressure swing is not a closed-gas Boyle calculation.

title: 3D Atlas: Alveolar Cup, Capillary Mesh & Fick’s Law of Diffusion
question: How does a 0.5 µm alveolar–capillary barrier transfer 250 mL of O₂ per minute at rest and up to 4,000 mL min⁻¹ during exercise?
explanation: Exploding the 3D alveolar sac and its wrapping capillary basket shows red blood cells squeezing single-file past squamous Type I pneumocytes, maximising surface area A (~70 m²) and minimising barrier thickness Δx (~0.5 µm) in Fick’s law.
limits: Steady-state alveolar–arterial partial pressure gradient.

title: 3D Atlas: Harvey’s One-Way Venous Valves & Quantitative Cardiac Output
question: How did William Harvey use simple multiplication of stroke volume by heart rate—plus forearm vein valves—to refute Galen’s tidal blood theory?
explanation: Inspecting the 3D semilunar venous valve leaflets and cardiac output readout (Q = HR × SV ≈ 5 L min⁻¹) shows why blood must circulate in a closed one-way loop.
limits: Coupled cardiac output and venous valve geometry.

title: 3D Atlas: Pulmonary & Systemic Figure-of-Eight Double Circulation
question: Why do mammals and birds route blood through the heart twice on every complete circuit of the body?
explanation: Tracing the blue pulmonary loop and red systemic loop in 3D shows why a double pump is essential: after blood loses pressure crossing the delicate pulmonary capillaries, the thick left ventricle re-pressurises oxygenated blood to 120 mmHg for systemic delivery.
limits: Simplified figure-of-eight vascular loop coupled to the four-chamber heart.

title: 3D Atlas: Four-Chamber Heart Cutaway & One-Way Valve Cycle
question: Why is the muscular wall of the left ventricle three times thicker than the right ventricle, and what makes the ‘lub-dub’ heart sounds?
explanation: Slicing the 3D heart in Section mode reveals the 12 mm left ventricular myocardium versus the 4 mm right wall, plus the atrioventricular (‘lub’) and semilunar (‘dub’) valves snapping shut under reverse pressure gradients.
limits: Synchronised cardiac cycle driven by heart-rate slider.

title: 3D Atlas: Artery Elastic Wall, Vein Semilunar Valve & Capillary Pore
question: How do the wall layers and lumen diameters of arteries, veins, and capillaries match their local blood pressures and flow velocities?
explanation: Comparing the three 3D vessel cylinders side-by-side shows thick elastic/smooth-muscle tunica media in high-pressure arteries, wide lumens with pocket valves in low-pressure veins, and a single-cell endothelium in exchange capillaries.
limits: Cross-sectional segments normalized for direct wall-thickness comparison.

title: 3D Atlas: Single-File Biconcave Erythrocytes & Capillary Tissue Exchange
question: Why does a human red blood cell eject its nucleus and squeeze single-file through a 7 µm capillary lumen?
explanation: Biconcave red cells have a short diffusion distance and flex through narrow capillaries. Loss of the nucleus leaves room for haemoglobin. Oxygen diffusion and net fluid filtration are separate processes; lymphatics return net filtered fluid.
limits: Focuses on erythrocytes and plasma flow inside the vessel trio.

title: 3D Atlas: Interventricular Septum & Left-to-Right Shunt Mechanics
question: Why does a hole in the muscular interventricular septum (VSD) force oxygenated blood from the left ventricle into the right ventricle rather than the reverse?
explanation: Slicing the 3D heart to inspect the interventricular septum shows that left ventricular systolic pressure (120 mmHg) is nearly five times right ventricular pressure (25 mmHg), driving a left-to-right shunt that overloads pulmonary capillaries.
limits: Assumed uncomplicated postnatal left-to-right shunt; pulmonary flow increases without an assumed fall in systemic oxygen saturation.

title: 3D Atlas: Point-to-Point Synaptic Signalling vs Broadcast Hormones
question: How does a 0.5 ms neurotransmitter pulse across a 20 nm synaptic cleft compare with blood-borne hormone signalling?
explanation: Compare signals routed through neural connections with blood-borne hormones acting on cells with suitable receptors. Neural and hormonal onset and duration vary, and both systems can work together.
limits: Focused on the 20 nm cleft geometry and receptor specificity. The relay is an excitatory chemical example; presynaptic regulation and inhibitory synapses also exist.

title: 3D Atlas: Sensory, Relay & Motor Neurone Architecture in the Reflex Arc
question: How does a spinal reflex arc trigger muscle withdrawal before the conscious cortex even registers pain?
explanation: Inspecting the 3D myelinated neurone and synaptic relay shows how routing a nociceptive spike directly from sensory neurone → spinal relay interneurone → motor neurone cuts conduction path length and synaptic delay.
limits: 3D myelinated motor neurone and synaptic junction. Waveforms are schematic, not an integration of Hodgkin–Huxley equations.

title: 3D Atlas: Myelinated Axon, Nodes of Ranvier & Saltatory Conduction
question: How does wrapping an axon in insulating Schwann-cell myelin speed action potentials from 2 m s⁻¹ up to 90 m s⁻¹ while saving metabolic energy?
explanation: Exploding the 3D motor neurone shows Schwann myelin sheaths preventing transmembrane current leak across internodes so the depolarising wave leaps node-to-node across voltage-gated Na⁺ channels studied by Obaid Siddiqi.
limits: Hodgkin–Huxley style travelling wave along discrete nodal segments. Waveforms are schematic, not an integration of Hodgkin–Huxley equations.

title: 3D Atlas: Ca²⁺-Triggered Synaptic Vesicle Exocytosis across the 20 nm Cleft
question: Why can nerve impulses cross a chemical synapse in only one direction, and how is the electrical signal converted to chemical and back?
explanation: Inspect presynaptic release and postsynaptic reception in this excitatory chemical relay. Presynaptic regulatory receptors and inhibitory synapses also exist; this drawing isolates one forward route.
limits: Quantal vesicle release scaled to stimulus threshold. The relay is an excitatory chemical example; presynaptic regulation and inhibitory synapses also exist.

title: 3D Atlas: Axonal Conduction Velocity vs Synaptic Delay Budget
question: Which stages contribute delay between a receptor signal and muscle activation?
explanation: Trace axonal propagation separately from chemical release, diffusion and postsynaptic responses. The drawn withdrawal circuit has two central junctions plus a neuromuscular junction. A chosen time budget does not measure hot-pan withdrawal.
limits: Illustrative timing depends on chosen inputs; no universal reflex latency.

title: 3D Atlas: Sectioned Human Eyeball, Fovea Cone Pit & Optic Disc
question: Why is colour acuity sharpest dead-centre on the fovea while the optic disc creates a complete blind spot?
explanation: Slicing the 3D eyeball in Section cutaway mode reveals the cornea, iris, crystalline lens, and posterior retina with the high-cone-density foveal pit and axon-packed optic nerve head.
limits: Thin-lens optical ray bundle to the fovea.

title: 3D Atlas: Ciliary Muscle Ring, Suspensory Ligaments & Lens Accommodation
question: Why does contracting the ciliary muscle make the suspensory ligaments go slack and the crystalline lens bulge thicker for near reading?
explanation: At near viewing distance the ciliary muscle contracts, ligament tension falls and the lens becomes more convex. At 25 cm the chosen 17 mm reduced-eye model needs about 62.82 D total eye power; this is not the lens power alone.
limits: Thin-lens vergence model (1/f = 1/u + 1/v) with 17 mm retinal distance.

title: 3D Atlas: PIN3 Auxin Redistribution, Acid Growth & Phototropic Curvature
question: How does a plant coleoptile bend toward unilateral blue light without a single muscle or neurone?
explanation: Shining directional light on the 3D coleoptile tip redistributes indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) to the shaded flank; proton pumps acidify the shaded cell walls, activating expansins so turgor elongates the shaded side faster and bends the shoot toward the light.
limits: Cholodny–Went differential elongation beam model.

title: 3D Atlas: Voltage-Gated Na⁺ Channel Blockade at Nodes of Ranvier
question: How does pufferfish tetrodotoxin (TTX) or Siddiqi’s para mutation silence nerve conduction without altering resting K⁺ leak?
explanation: Dropping stimulus efficacy below threshold at the 3D Nodes of Ranvier demonstrates how plugging voltage-gated Na⁺ channels prevents the regenerative depolarising upstroke while leaving the −70 mV resting potential intact.
limits: Threshold-gated nodal Na⁺ current model. Waveforms are schematic, not an integration of Hodgkin–Huxley equations.

title: 3D Atlas: Pancreatic Islet β/α Cells & GLUT4 Vesicle Translocation
question: How does insulin secreted by pancreatic β-cells open the glucose door on muscle and liver membranes after a carbohydrate meal?
explanation: Raising blood glucose above 90 mg dL⁻¹ in the 3D islet station triggers β-cell insulin exocytosis; insulin binding to its tyrosine-kinase receptor translocates intracellular GLUT4 vesicles into the plasma membrane, accelerating glucose uptake and glycogen synthesis.
limits: Steady-state insulin/glucagon ratio and GLUT4 membrane insertion fraction. Illustrative assumptions; rates and volumes are not individual clinical predictions.

title: 3D Atlas: Cutaneous Arteriolar Vasomotion, Eccrine Sweat & Piloerection
question: How does a 2 mm layer of human skin switch between a heat radiator in summer and a thermal insulator in winter?
explanation: Slicing the 3D dermis while sweeping ambient temperature shows hypothalamic sympathetic control dilating superficial arteriolar loops and activating coiled eccrine sweat glands in heat, or constricting arterioles and contracting arrector pili muscles in cold.
limits: Coupled radiative/convective and evaporative dermal heat flux model. Illustrative assumptions; rates and volumes are not individual clinical predictions.

title: 3D Atlas: Evaporative Sweat Cooling vs High-Humidity Heat Balance
question: Why is a 38 °C day when dry heat evaporates sweat instantly far safer than a humid coastal afternoon when sweat drips off unevaporated?
explanation: Driving ambient temperature above 37 °C in the 3D skin block shows radiative heat transfer reversing inward, leaving latent heat of sweat evaporation (2,420 kJ L⁻¹) from eccrine ducts as the body’s sole cooling channel.
limits: Dermal heat balance model. Illustrative assumptions; rates and volumes are not individual clinical predictions.

title: 3D Atlas: Hepatic Deamination & Renal Clearance of Urea
question: Why must excess amino acids be deaminated in the liver and converted into urea before the kidneys filter them out?
explanation: Following urea through the 3D glomerulus and nephron tubule shows how the liver converts toxic ammonia (NH₃) into neutral, highly water-soluble urea that passes freely through Bowman’s capsule for urinary excretion.
limits: Glomerular and tubular urea clearance view. Illustrative assumptions; rates and volumes are not individual clinical predictions.

title: 3D Atlas: Glomerular Ultrafiltration, Loop of Henle & Aquaporin-2
question: Why do human kidneys filter 180 L of plasma every day only to reabsorb 99% of it along the nephron tubule?
explanation: Following the 3D nephron from Bowman’s capsule through the proximal tubule, countercurrent Loop of Henle (300 → 1,200 mOsm L⁻¹), and ADH-regulated collecting duct shows how high filtration plus selective reabsorption purges urea while normally recovering nearly all glucose and ~99% of water.
limits: Steady-state GFR (125 mL min⁻¹) and ADH-dependent collecting-duct water reabsorption. Illustrative assumptions; rates and volumes are not individual clinical predictions.

title: 3D Atlas: Cholera Toxin Cl⁻ Efflux & Mahalanabis’s SGLT1 ORS Rescue
question: Why does adding equimolar glucose to salt water allow a cholera-stricken gut to absorb water when plain saline fails?
explanation: Inspecting the 3D tubular cotransport and antibody defence stages shows how SGLT1 Na⁺–glucose symporters remain intact during cholera toxin secretion, pulling Na⁺, glucose, and osmotic water back into the bloodstream.
limits: Represented via tubular Na⁺/glucose cotransport and mucosal immunity. Illustrative assumptions; rates and volumes are not individual clinical predictions.

title: 3D Atlas: Y-Shaped IgG Antibody Hinge, Fab Paratopes & Vaccine Memory
question: How can one class of Y-shaped IgG protein both lock onto millions of distinct pathogen epitopes and flag them for macrophages?
explanation: Exploding the 3D IgG heterotetramer reveals two heavy and two light chains linked by disulphide bridges: hypervariable Fab tips clamp complementary pathogen epitopes while the conserved Fc stem recruits phagocytes and complement.
limits: Flexible hinge angle shown locking onto a spherical viral capsid. Illustrative assumptions; rates and volumes are not individual clinical predictions.

title: 3D Atlas: Pre-Formed Antivenom IgG vs Clonal Memory B-Cell Immunity
question: Why does a snakebite victim need immediate passive IgG antivenom infusion rather than an active vaccine?
explanation: Inspecting the 3D IgG Fab–antigen lock shows that passive immunity supplies pre-made antibodies immediately (0-day lag) to neutralise circulating toxin, though without generating memory B cells.
limits: Direct 3D IgG neutralisation complex. Illustrative assumptions; rates and volumes are not individual clinical predictions.

title: 3D Atlas: Hyperglycaemia, PCT SGLT Saturation & Osmotic Diuresis
question: Why does untreated diabetes mellitus (>180 mg dL⁻¹ blood glucose) cause glucose to spill into urine (glycosuria) and pull excess water with it?
explanation: Sliding blood glucose up to 240 mg dL⁻¹ in the 3D Islet and Nephron stations saturates the proximal convoluted tubule’s SGLT symporters, leaving un-reabsorbed glucose in the filtrate where it opposes osmotic water reabsorption in the collecting duct.
limits: Coupled islet GLUT4 and nephron tubular transport threshold model. Illustrative assumptions; rates and volumes are not individual clinical predictions.
